sections.title: The limit point set of real roots of random polynomials: a resolution of Erdős Problem 521
sections.abstract: For i.i.d. real coefficients of mean zero, variance one, and a finite absolute exponential moment, the authors determine the almost-sure liminf, limsup, and complete interval of subsequential limits for the real-root count of Kac polynomials divided by log n.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove almost surely that the normalized number of distinct real roots has liminf 1/π, limsup 1/π+C*, and every value in between as a subsequential limit; C*>1/π is defined by an entropy-one equation. The lower-limit identity holds under a finite 2+δ moment, while the full limit-set statement uses the stronger exponential-moment hypothesis.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: One infinite i.i.d. sequence of real, mean-zero, variance-one coefficients; finite absolute exponential moment for the full interval theorem. For the lower endpoint alone, a finite 2+δ moment suffices.
sections.unique_caveat: The exact upper endpoint and full interval are not established under only the weaker 2+δ moment assumption.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The abstract claims a resolution of a named, longstanding problem and gives an explicit almost-sure limit set. The independent Erdős Problems record #521 confirms the historical question being addressed; the paper's own introduction explains the stronger limit-set result.

sections.title: A complete solution to the Naor isomorphic reverse isoperimetry conjecture
sections.abstract: For every origin-symmetric convex body in R^n, the authors find a volume-preserving linear image containing a nearby symmetric convex body whose isoperimetric quotient is at most 40 ε^-1√n, resolving Naor's conjecture.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove that for every origin-symmetric convex body K⊂R^n there is T∈SL_n(R) such that, for each ε∈(0,1), an origin-symmetric L exists with (1−ε)TK⊆L⊆TK and iq(L)≤40 ε^-1√n.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Finite-dimensional R^n, origin-symmetric convex bodies, and a volume-preserving linear transformation; the approximation parameter ε is strictly between 0 and 1.
sections.unique_caveat: The quantitative guarantee depends on ε through ε^-1; the theorem is an isomorphic, approximate-body statement, not an exact bound for TK itself.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper states an explicit resolution for every origin-symmetric convex body, with quantitative constants. Search results surfaced Naor's earlier source for the conjecture, providing context for the claimed target; the introduction and Theorem 1.1 give the hypotheses and bound.

sections.title: The coercivity conjecture for nonlocal energies
sections.abstract: The authors disprove a general implication from ellipticity to fractional Sobolev coercivity for symmetric nonlocal kernels in much of the parameter range, while proving coercivity for selected kernel classes via annular cancellation.
sections.claimed_result: The authors show that the conjectured coercivity fails when n>2s, including for smooth compactly supported tests, and holds for n=1, s>1/2. They also establish a local coercivity criterion based on annular cancellation, derive results for several kernel classes, and obtain Hölder estimates under ellipticity and cancellation assumptions.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Symmetric measurable nonlocal kernels of order 2s, 0<s<1, satisfying the paper's upper and directional lower ellipticity conditions; positive results require additional cancellation or class-specific hypotheses.
sections.unique_caveat: Ellipticity alone is insufficient in the counterexample regime, and the positive results do not assert coercivity for every kernel in the remaining parameter range.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The abstract pairs a counterexample to a central coercivity conjecture with positive criteria and an application to the Gressman–Strain estimate. This is a particularly broad result within its stated kernel framework; the introduction specifies the ellipticity conditions.

sections.title: A counterexample to fixed-profile soliton resolution for the three-dimensional quintic wave equation
sections.abstract: For the three-dimensional focusing energy-critical wave equation, the authors construct a bounded forward-global solution near a sign-changing stationary state whose stationary core has two distinct similarity-orbit limits, contradicting a fixed-profile resolution assertion.
sections.claimed_result: The authors construct a bounded forward-global solution, arbitrarily close initially to a sign-changing stationary state, asymptotic to a varying stationary profile plus a free wave; two separated similarity-orbit limits rule out any fixed finite list of stationary profiles for the stated full-time resolution assertion.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The focusing energy-critical equation u_tt−Δu=u^5 on [0,∞)×R^3 in the energy space; the construction has a specified odd symmetry and concerns the fixed-profile quantifier order described in the paper.
sections.unique_caveat: This refutes the stated fixed-profile formulation, not every weaker or sequence-dependent formulation of soliton resolution.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The abstract and Theorem 1.1 state a concrete counterexample to a precise version of soliton resolution. Its construction combines controlled radiation with a computer-assisted certificate for the stationary state and its odd energy kernel.

sections.title: Forbidden subset sums in a linear range: an inverse theorem and the Erdős-Graham irregularity problem
sections.abstract: The author studies the largest subset of {1,…,⌊cn⌋} avoiding a distinct-element sum of n, proves an exact formula for c≥1 and limit-point results for c<1, and gives an inverse theorem for subset sums.
sections.claimed_result: For c≥1, f_c(n)=⌊cn⌋−⌈n/2⌉; for 0<c<1, the normalized sequence fails to converge and has multiple limit points, including the exact set {1/6,1/4} at c=1/2. An inverse theorem supplies a uniform sufficient condition for a subset sum, with some results machine-checked in Lean 4.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: f_c(n) maximizes |A| over A⊆{1,…,⌊cn⌋} for which n is not a sum of distinct elements; the inverse theorem has additional parameters and range restrictions stated in the abstract.
sections.unique_caveat: The formalized portion is only a subset of the results (notably cases with q∈{2,3}); the broader asymptotic statements remain author-reported proofs in the preprint.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The abstract gives exact and asymptotic results for a named Erdős–Graham problem and reports Lean 4 formalization for several specified subclaims; the paper also bridges combinatorics and number theory.

sections.title: The Brown--Shields Conjecture: Two Approximation Theorems and a Counterexample
sections.abstract: The authors construct an outer function in the classical Dirichlet space whose radial zero set has logarithmic capacity zero but whose polynomial multiples do not approximate 1, disproving the Brown–Shields conjecture.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove that a counterexample can be built with an outer Dirichlet-space function whose radial zero set is polar, and show that counterexamples of this type approximate every proper outer canonical generator in both Dirichlet norm and boundary-log L^1 norm.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Classical Dirichlet space and its canonical generators; the construction uses a complete metric and a nested-ball argument to preserve outerness and noncyclicity.
sections.unique_caveat: The arXiv comments identify this as an expository version with navigational aids, not intended for publication; its result is a counterexample rather than a full replacement characterization of cyclicity.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The abstract reports a direct counterexample to a named conjecture plus two approximation theorems that support the construction; it specifies a strong capacity-zero property for the zero set.

sections.title: A constructive computer-assisted existence proof for a Calabi--Yau metric
sections.abstract: The authors give a rigorous constructive proof of a Ricci-flat Kähler metric on the Fermat quartic, combining numerical approximation, a fixed-point theorem, and verified bounds.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove constructively that the Fermat quartic admits a Ricci-flat Kähler metric and provide an explicit accurate analytic approximation, using computation to obtain an approximate solution and verified numerics to close a fixed-point argument.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The specific Fermat quartic hypersurface and the authors' validated computational bounds; broader manifolds are discussed as future applications of the method.
sections.unique_caveat: The existence theorem is established for the stated example; the abstract does not establish that the method is already effective for other manifolds.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: This is a constructive, computer-assisted existence claim for a central geometric object, with verified numerics and a cross-list in high-energy theory; the abstract explicitly distinguishes the approach from relying on Yau's existence theorem.
